name: Adjective ending after an article
english: An adjective in front of a noun always takes an ending. After ein/eine the ending carries the gender information.
explanation: An adjective in front of a noun always takes an ending. After ein/eine the ending carries the gender information.

name: Dative after a preposition
english: Some prepositions always take dative. The article changes, not the noun.
explanation: Some prepositions always take dative. The article changes, not the noun.

name: Two-way preposition: motion or place
english: The same preposition takes accusative for motion towards, dative for position. in die Luft (where to) vs in der Luft (where).
explanation: The same preposition takes accusative for motion towards, dative for position. in die Luft (where to) vs in der Luft (where).

name: Comparative and superlative
english: -er for more, -st for most, plus the adjective ending. Short adjectives often take an umlaut.
explanation: -er for more, -st for most, plus the adjective ending. Short adjectives often take an umlaut.

name: Genitive for possession
english: der/die/das becomes des/der, and masculine and neuter nouns add -s or -es.
explanation: der/die/das becomes des/der, and masculine and neuter nouns add -s or -es.

name: Imperative
english: The du-form drops the pronoun and usually the -st ending; the verb opens the sentence.
explanation: The du-form drops the pronoun and usually the -st ending; the verb opens the sentence.

name: Modal verb + infinitive at the end
english: The modal takes the personal ending in second position; the main verb waits, unconjugated, at the end of the clause.
explanation: The modal takes the personal ending in second position; the main verb waits, unconjugated, at the end of the clause.

name: Passive with werden
english: werden is conjugated in second position, the past participle goes to the very end. Everything else sits between them.
explanation: werden is conjugated in second position, the past participle goes to the very end. Everything else sits between them.

name: Strong verb in the simple past
english: The vowel changes instead of adding -te. These have to be recognised, not derived.
explanation: The vowel changes instead of adding -te. These have to be recognised, not derived.

name: Reflexive verb with accusative sich
english: The verb needs sich to be complete. It is not translated in English, and it is not optional.
explanation: The verb needs sich to be complete. It is not translated in English, and it is not optional.

name: Reflexive with dative sich
english: When the sentence already has an accusative object, sich becomes dative: she washed the face to herself.
explanation: When the sentence already has an accusative object, sich becomes dative: she washed the face to herself.

name: Separable verb, prefix split off
english: In a main clause the prefix detaches and travels to the end of the sentence, sometimes many words away from its verb.
explanation: In a main clause the prefix detaches and travels to the end of the sentence, sometimes many words away from its verb.

name: Verb in second position
english: When something other than the subject opens the sentence, the verb still comes second and the subject moves behind it.
explanation: When something other than the subject opens the sentence, the verb still comes second and the subject moves behind it.

name: Perfect tense with sein
english: Movement and change-of-state verbs often form the perfect with sein.
explanation: The finite form of sein is in second position; the past participle closes the clause.

name: Subordinate clause with dass
english: In a dass-clause, the conjugated verb moves to the end.
explanation: The conjunction dass opens a subordinate clause and sends the finite verb to the clause-final position.

name: Accusative + infinitive perception
english: sehen/hören + object + infinitive
explanation: After sehen or hören, the object can be followed directly by an infinitive: Ich sehe ihn gehen.

name: Subordinate clause with dass
english: dass sends the finite verb to the end
explanation: A dass-clause reports a thought or statement. The conjugated verb moves to the end.

name: Subordinate clause: verb final
english: A subordinate conjunction sends the verb to the end
explanation: With bevor, während, als, wenn and similar conjunctions, the conjugated verb closes the clause.

name: Reason with weil
english: weil sends the finite verb to the end
explanation: Use weil to give a reason. The conjugated verb goes to the end of the clause.

name: Indirect question
english: Question word + verb at the end
explanation: In an indirect question, the question word opens the clause and the finite verb goes to the end.

name: Infinitive with zu
english: zu + infinitive after verbs such as bitten and versuchen
explanation: Many verbs introduce another action with zu + infinitive.

name: Indirect yes/no question with ob
english: ob sends the finite verb to the end
explanation: Use ob for an indirect yes/no question. The finite verb goes to the end.

name: Conditional with würde
english: würde + infinitive
explanation: Use würde + infinitive for a hypothetical action.

name: Purpose with um ... zu
english: um + object + zu + infinitive
explanation: Use um ... zu to say why someone does something. The infinitive closes the phrase.

name: Relative clause with was
english: alles, was ...
explanation: After alles or etwas, was can introduce a relative clause.

name: Time with während
english: während sends the verb to the end
explanation: Use während for two actions happening at the same time.

name: Comparison with als ob
english: so tun, als ob ...
explanation: Als ob introduces an unreal comparison; the verb goes to the end.

name: Condition or repeated time with wenn
english: wenn sends the verb to the end
explanation: Use wenn for a condition or repeated event. The finite verb closes the clause.

name: One past event with als
english: als sends the verb to the end
explanation: Use als for a single event in the past. The finite verb goes to the end.

name: Relative clause with der/die/das
english: A relative pronoun refers back to a noun
explanation: The relative pronoun carries gender and case; the finite verb goes to the end.

name: Past hypothetical
english: wäre / hätte + participle
explanation: Use wäre or hätte with a past participle for an unreal past possibility.

name: Past perfect
english: hatte/war + past participle
explanation: The past perfect describes an event that happened before another past event.
